knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A ground-contact post needs a timber whose data names a ground-contact class [QLD-TIMBER]. Treatment is not all the same, and an above-ground label is not suitable here.
Some treatments corrode standard fixings, which can lead to a joint failing after the work is finished.
A load-carrying connection needs a fixing rated for the load and fixed into the structure. A surface screw does not meet that need.

practicalCriteria: Selects timber, treatment class and fixings for three sample exposures (ground contact, exposed above-ground rail, and a load-carrying connection), and records a supplier data reference for each.
Identifies and rejects at least one above-ground product used in ground contact, and one fixing that is not rated for its treatment, citing the supplier data in each case.
Completes the material and fixing records correctly, without stating a treatment, rating or method that the supplier data does not give.
passRule: Assessor review of the material and fixing records and an observed selection for the three sample exposures, with all three practical criteria met. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Material record with product name, grade, treatment class and data reference
Fixing record with rating and manufacturer data reference
Photographs of product labels, with permission where a site is used
stopWorkCriteria: A timber without a ground-contact class is set in the ground
A load-carrying connection is made with surface fixings alone
An unidentified preservative or unlabelled product is in use
A structural connection is changed on site without a referral
